title: Publish the discrepancies and a reconciliation summary
prompt:
The finance team needs one list of everything that doesn't reconcile, so someone can look at each item. Write `reconciliation_exceptions(accounts, transactions, transfers, ledger_entries)`. It returns one row per problem, from the three sources below, with the columns of `EXCEPTION_SCHEMA`.

`reconciliation_summary` is already written: it counts your exceptions by kind. When this step passes, press Run project to see every table of the pipeline, the two balances side by side included.
rules: Every transfer in `transfer_matches` whose `match_status` isn't `matched`: `kind` is its status, `ref_id` its `transfer_id`, `account_id` its `from_account_id`, `amount` its `amount`.
Every ledger entry whose `transfer_id` isn't in `transfers`, or is missing: `kind` is `unknown_transfer`, `ref_id` its `entry_id`, with its own `account_id` and `amount`.

Every account in `account_balances` whose `difference` isn't zero: `kind` is `balance_difference`, `ref_id` and `account_id` are its `account_id`, `amount` is the difference. A difference of 0.01 is listed.
Return `kind`, `ref_id`, `account_id` and `amount`, with `amount` as `decimal(14,2)`. When everything reconciles, the result is empty.
hints: Build the three parts separately, each a `select` with `.alias` into `kind`, `ref_id`, `account_id` and `amount`. `F.lit("unknown_transfer")` makes a fixed column.
A left anti join of `ledger_entries` with `transfers.select("transfer_id")` keeps the entries whose transfer doesn't exist. A missing `transfer_id` never matches, so those entries are kept too.
`unionByName` stacks the parts by column name. Cast `amount` to `MONEY` in each part so every row has the same type.
explanation: Each source of trouble is already a table: `transfer_matches` names every transfer that isn't clean, a left anti join finds ledger entries that belong to no transfer, and `account_balances` shows where the two balances part ways. Shaping each into the same four columns and stacking them with `unionByName` gives one list the team can work through, matching columns by name rather than position. The balance filter is `difference != 0`, with no tolerance: a one-cent gap is exactly the kind of error a reconciliation exists to catch. The transfer rows explain the balance rows: a duplicate shows up on both accounts it touched, a missing credit on the receiver, a cent mismatch as a cent. On balanced books the list is empty, which is what the summary should show before the books close.
